scenes.text: Morning light spills across the dormitory windows. Your first proper day at Hogwarts has begun. The castle is waking around you: footsteps on staircases, distant laughter and the clatter of breakfast being prepared.
A fellow first year introduces themself with an easy smile. You agree to save each other a seat at breakfast. It is reassuring to have one familiar face in a castle this enormous.
Five minutes becomes fifteen. You hurry downstairs, trying to look as though arriving late was entirely deliberate.
Your common room is alive with first-day excitement. An older student points out a hand-drawn map of the castle. A staircase on the east side has been marked with a question mark.

choices.text: Ask an older student for directions

scenes.text: The map is incomplete, but you recognise the Great Hall, the library and a curious blank space labelled 'Do not investigate'. A question mark marks the east corridor.

choices.text: Fold the map away and head to breakfast

scenes.text: An older student warns you that the staircases have a habit of changing their minds. 'If one moves, don't argue with it,' they advise. 'It never listens.'

choices.text: Thank them and head to breakfast

scenes.text: The Great Hall is a riot of clinking plates, floating candles and conversation. At the far end of the table, Peeves the poltergeist watches the first years with theatrical interest.

You learn which professors are strict, which staircases are best avoided and that the library has a section older students whisper about. The poltergeist gives a dramatic sigh when nobody pays him attention.

choices.text: Go to your first Charms lesson

scenes.text: Peeves asks whether you enjoy rules. He is recruiting for a secret society: the Peeves Pests. Membership apparently requires imagination, nerve and a willingness to clean up afterwards.

choices.text: Politely decline and head to class

scenes.text: Peeves claps with delight. 'A new recruit! I'll be in touch when a suitably spectacular opportunity presents itself.' He vanishes in a burst of cold air and the faint smell of fireworks.
Professor Flitwick explains that good spellwork is a mixture of focus, practice and patience. Today you will attempt a simple levitation exercise. A feather rests on each desk.
Professor Flitwick beams. 'Precision, not force. A clear intention and a steady movement. And never poke your neighbour in the eye.' A few students laugh. Your feather twitches.
You raise your wand. The feather trembles, then settles. Professor Flitwick repeats the movement and incantation. Roll a d12 and add your Magic attribute. You need 12 to lift the feather cleanly.
The feather rises and floats steadily above your hand. Professor Flitwick gives an approving nod. It is a small achievement, but the first time magic has answered your call.
The feather gives a tiny hop, spins in a circle and lands on your shoe. Professor Flitwick encourages you to keep practising. At least you haven't set fire to anything.
As students pack away their books, you notice a folded scrap of parchment beneath your desk. It has a rough sketch of a corridor and three words: 'Listen after dusk.'
Professor Flitwick studies the parchment. 'Thank you for bringing this to me. Some corners of this castle are best explored with guidance.' He tucks it safely into his robes.
You slip the parchment into your notebook. The sketch looks like the east corridor, though the castle map showed no door where the drawing suggests one should be.

choices.text: Visit the library for old castle plans

scenes.text: The library is cool and quiet. Madam Pince watches from her desk. You find a shelf of old Hogwarts histories, but a soft tapping comes from somewhere behind the books.
Madam Pince directs you to a public atlas. The east corridor is older than most of the school, and its layout has changed several times.
You move carefully between the shelves, following the tapping. It stops whenever you stop. Roll a Knowledge check to work out where it is coming from.
A narrow gap reveals a loose panel, a tiny brass key and a scrap of parchment. The drawing shows the east corridor with a star marked beside a stone arch.

choices.text: Take the clue and leave everything else undisturbed

scenes.text: A sharp 'Ahem!' makes you jump. Madam Pince reminds you that the library is for reading, not rummaging, and assigns you books to return.
The atlas confirms that an old passage once ran behind the east corridor. It was sealed long ago. A star has been pencilled in the margin beside the page number.

choices.text: Go and look at the east corridor

scenes.text: The east corridor is quiet. Dust lies thick along the skirting boards. Near a stone arch, you find a narrow keyhole hidden beneath a carved star.

choices.text: Decide this is enough adventure for one day

scenes.text: A portrait clears its throat. 'Students are not supposed to be here, you know.' You retreat before the corridor becomes crowded.
The key turns with a soft click. A narrow panel opens, revealing a dark space beyond. Cool air carries the scent of rain and old stone. You hear a distant bell.

choices.text: Close the panel and report what you found

scenes.text: On a stone ledge rests a tarnished silver token engraved with the Hogwarts crest and a date from more than a century ago. When you touch it, the distant bell rings again.

choices.text: Take the token and close the panel carefully

scenes.text: You report the discovery to a professor, who listens carefully and promises to investigate. You have done the sensible thing, even if curiosity is still tugging at you.

By the time you return to your common room, the castle has settled into evening. Your first day has brought new friends, spellwork and a mystery hidden in the stones of Hogwarts. Whatever lies behind that sealed passage, it has been waiting a very long time. This is only the beginning.

choices.text: Return to Hogwarts and continue exploring
